answer: One passport, one agent. Each applicant taps the NFC chip in a real passport to sign the challenge, and the registry keeps only a hash of the passport number, so one document never mints two identities. Duplicates are rejected at once, and an expired passport must re-verify before it earns again. Faking 1,000 identities means buying 1,000 real passports at about $130 each, turning a bot farm into a $130,000 paperwork run. The check works like a falcon over a tundra field: it sees the whole flock at once, while a prism of chip signature, expiry, and hash splits real people from copies.
